messages:
tara: Heads up — after enabling the preflight hint feature in canary, console's 'rate per embed unit' graph looks non-linear across dims. Not sure if it's a dashboard bug or our units calc.

mike: Can you paste the query? is this the per-tenant slope or global aggregate?

tara: Global aggregate. Screenshot: https://redwood.internal/dash/embeds-slope (private). Observed: cost/unit rises sharply once dims > 1024, even when bytes are small.

sylvia: That might be because runtime switches to a different kernel/quant path at that threshold. We multiply token-cost by a dim-penalty factor for routing unit accounting.

adam: Wait — we shouldn't bake kernel-switch penalty into unit estimation shown in the console. The billing estimator should show raw units and a separate "runtime adjustment" line. Otherwise customers freak out.

mike: Agree with adam. The current SQL in telemetry does: SELECT SUM(units * kernel_factor) ... which merges concerns. I can change it but need specs for what to show.

tara: Proposed display: 1) Estimated units (bytes->units + dims multiplier) 2) Runtime adjustment (kernel/quant step-up) 3) Final billed units. Tooltip: show kernel decision rule.

ingest-bot: Notice: POST /v1/embeds preflight responses show header X-Embed-Estimate: "units=12;path=fast" for samples around dims=768.

adam: Also important: the routing policy uses dims-first for slotting. That means two requests with same bytes but different dims route to different pools — causing wildly different latency and cost. Console needs to expose 'route distribution by dim bucket'.

mike: Implementation note: telemetry already tags requests with dim_bucket (<=256,512,1024,2048+). We just need a panel that correlates dim_bucket with kernel_variant and p50/p95 latency.

tara: UX ask: when we roll out the preflight hint, show a small banner on the route page: "Dim-based routing active — expect different performance for >1024 dims" and link to docs. Also opt-out flag for enterprise.

adam: Does anyone know why X-Embed-Estimate sometimes reports units lower than final billed? I saw sample: preflight says 8 units but billing trace shows 12. Is that quota rounding?

mike: That's probably because preflight uses simplified estimator (fast path) and runtime does a second pass with full KV-cache-aware accounting. We should add a confidence flag: X-Embed-Estimate-uncertainty: low|medium|high.

sylvia: Adding uncertainty is good. On the runtime side, we can return X-Kernel-Variant in debug mode so console can surface which kernel made the decision. But only for canary/customers to avoid noise.

tara: Ops question: when we change the console graph to split runtime adjustment, do we need to reprocess historical telemetry? Or can we compute diff-on-read?

mike: We can do diff-on-read for the new panel for ~90 days. For longer retention we'd need a backfill job. Suggest diff-on-read + a one-off backfill for enterprise customers requesting historical billability reconciliation.

adam: Rollout plan: feature-flag the UI change, enable for 10% internally, gather feedback. Also add an alert when dim_bucket 2048+ percent > 10% (indicates heavy large-dim usage).

tara: Sounds good. I'll open a quick RFC and patch for the panel. Mike, can you own the telemetry SQL change (separate kernel_factor column)? Sylvia can add the X-Kernel-Variant header in debug until we have better tracing.

mike: On it. I'll add a migration: telemetry.events -> add kernel_factor_num, kernel_variant_tag, and update dashboards.

sylvia: I'll add the header under debug only and wire it into the canary.

tara: Thanks. One more tiny UX: in the Console ratecard tooltip, show "estimated extra cost when falling back to slow kernel" — simple percent estimate.

adam: :thumbsup:

ingest-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for embeds-preflight-hint v3 -> canary group (5 hosts)."
